title: Every save from a desk form copies and compares the gym's whole history several times
what: When the desk saves anything from these forms (add or edit a member, sell or renew, collect or cancel a payment, freeze, move a start date), the admin app first turns the whole gym (every member, plan, payment and every visit ever) into text, reads it back into a second copy, copies it again inside the save, compares every single row before and after, and then builds the whole gym again for the screens. A gym with 500 or more members and a year of check-ins means tens of thousands of rows handled about eight times for one tap. On a cheap desk phone this can show as a pause after pressing Save that grows every month. It has not been measured: no speed test runs with a big gym.
expected: A save handles only the rows it changes, so pressing Save takes the same short time on day 1 and in year 3, and a speed test with a 500-member gym proves it.
who: front desk and owners of bigger gyms
how_often: every save from a desk form
fix_line: Run each save on just the member's own rows and time it with a 500-member test gym
